newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Interest turns light in Australian bond market.
newsitem.headline: Interest turns light in Australian bond market.

text.p: *Australian bonds were restricted to a narrow trading range during a slow moving session as the market awaited the re-opening of U.S. markets and key local data later this week.
*ANZ job ads rise 0.5 percent in June.
Australian bonds were restricted to a narrow trading range during a slow moving session in sharp contrast to the strong demand seen last week.

Traders said the market was largely awaiting the reopening of U.S. markets after Friday's Independence Day holiday, although U.S. Treasuries were showing an easier bias in Tokyo in response to a fall in the U.S. dollar.

The Tokyo market also latched onto comments by Australian Prime Minister John Howard saying Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan had told him in their recent meeting that the U.S. economy was stronger than he had ever seen.
Meanwhile, the local focus in firmly on this Thursday's June labour force report on which the outcome is seen deciding the market's thoughts on future monetary policy.

Economists are expecting a solid rebound in employment after the sharp fall in May, although they doubt it will make much of a dent in the current sluggishness of the labour market and have minimal impact on the high level of unemployment.

ANZ's June jobs advertisements data released earlier showed a 0.5 percent rise after the 7.3 percent fall in May. Commenting on the data ANZ chief economist Saul Eslake said: "Demand for labour is increasing, but at a fairly slow pace."

The local market gave up some ground to the U.S. and Canada after last week's general outperformance, although it held its ground against New Zealand. The yield curve was marginally flatter, continuing last week's trend after the Reserve Bank made no announcement on policy following the board meeting.

The 10-year bond contract tested the 3-1/2 year peak of 93.210 set in Friday's SYCOM session, although analysts feel the three-year contract has to play catch up to long end's recent advance before it can test resistance at 93.250.
